_notes: What `map-helper show` prints for each physical input: [glyph, name] per pad style, positional like everything else (docs/03). Emulators see Steam's virtual Xbox 360 pad, so a pad's south button is SDL's A whatever it says on it: on a Switch Pro or an 8BitDo in Nintendo style that button is marked B. A style lists only what differs from `generic`; `families` overrides a style for one family. `shapes` maps a controllers.json style to the drawing the UI uses; any other style is `generic`. `ls`/`rs` are the sticks as one input each. Paddle numbers are SDL's: PADDLE1 is the Xbox Elite's P1 (upper, under the right hand), PADDLE2 its P3 (upper left), PADDLE3 P2 (lower right), PADDLE4 P4 (lower left); on the Deck SDL reads R4, L4, R5, L5 into them. Which SDL paddle a two-paddle pad (8BitDo Ultimate 2, DualSense Edge) reports for each side is [VERIFY].
_sources: SDL release-2.30.0 include/SDL_gamecontroller.h L731-755 (button enum, MISC1 and PADDLE1-4 comments): https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/release-2.30.0/include/SDL_gamecontroller.h#L731-L755

SDL release-2.30.0 src/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_steamdeck.c L280-287 (R4, L4, R5, L5 -> PADDLE1-4): https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/release-2.30.0/src/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_steamdeck.c#L280-L287

The pads' own markings: DualShock 4 (Share, Options, PS), DualSense (Create, Options, PS, mic), Xbox (View, Menu, LB/RB, LT/RT), Switch Pro (B south, A east, Y west, X north, -, +, ZL/ZR, Home, Capture), Steam Deck (A/B/X/Y, L1/R1, L2/R2, View, Menu, L4/L5/R4/R5)

8bitdo.ultimate._source: Printed PL/PR on the owner's Ultimate 2 Wireless (2026-10-23); paddle1 = right as on other two-paddle pads [VERIFY]

_steam_only_notes: Inputs Steam's virtual pad doesn't have: it is an Xbox 360 pad (28de:11ff, 'Microsoft X-Box 360 pad N', data/controllers.json virtual_devices), with no paddles, share/mic/capture button or touchpad, so an emulator behind Steam Input never sees them. Steam Input can still map them to buttons the virtual pad has.
